title: quantization-nan-debug-scratchpad-maya-2026-03-22
content:
Quick notes / breadcrumbs from triage of NaN quality regressions after adding INT8 + FP8 quant paths. Mostly a scratchpad for me, leaving rough commands + outputs + hypotheses for follow-ups.

Summary:
- After enabling int8 quantized kernels for the decoder, several model runs produced NaN logits mid-generation (~step 12-20). Happens intermittently but reproducible on some test prompts.
- Suspect precision-mismatch / scaling bug between fp8 conversion and bf16 pathways or a kernel edge case with long KV cache reuse.

Observed behavior:
- 2026-03-18 14:03:12 UTC: model run on dedicated-GPU pool hit NaN at generation step 18, output: "logits[0,18,:] = nan". Token probabilities became NaN and sampler failed (ValueError in top-k).
- GPU logs: "WARN: kernel launch returned nan result for fused-attn" (runtime tag in metrics). No CUDA OOM.
- Reproduced on local devbox (A10) when using quantized-int8 + fp8-accel toggles; runs OK in bf16 baseline.

Commands tried (local repro):
- Baseline (bf16):
  python run_inference.py --model ./checkpoints/decoder_fp16 --dtype bf16 --batch 1 --max-tokens 128 --prompt-file examples/long-prompts.txt
  -> completes OK, no NaNs.

- Int8 quantize + run:
  python quantize.py --model ./checkpoints/decoder_fp16 --out ./checkpoints/decoder_int8 --scheme per_channel --calib-data data/calib-1000.jsonl
  python run_inference.py --model ./checkpoints/decoder_int8 --dtype int8 --enable-fp8-accel --batch 1 --max-tokens 128 --prompt-file examples/long-prompts.txt
  -> intermittent NaN at step ~12-20.

- Quick debug prints to isolate layer: added tensor checks after each decoder block in runtime loop:
  if torch.isnan(x).any(): logger.info(f"NaN after block {i}")
  -> NaN flagged after block 6 consistently for failing runs.

- Dumped weights/stats for block 6:
  - activation min/max pre-attn: [-3.2, 4.1]
  - attention scores mean/std: [0.05, 3.1] (std suspiciously high)
  - layernorm eps=1e-5 in bf16 baseline; in quant path the layernorm cast to float32 then back to int8 kernel paths?

- Tried toggles: per_tensor vs per_channel quantization, different clip thresholds, adjust layernorm eps from 1e-5 -> 1e-3. Results: increasing eps reduced frequency of NaNs but did not eliminate.

Recent test matrix (notes):
- int8 per_channel + fp8-accel: NaN 7/10 runs.
- int8 per_tensor + fp8-accel: NaN 4/10 runs.
- int8 per_channel without fp8-accel (force bf16 ops): 1/10 runs (much lower).
- bf16 baseline: 0/20 runs.

Hypotheses (ordered by suspicion):
1) FP8 casting/accumulation bug in fused attention kernels when mixed with INT8 weight representation. Some intermediate accumulation uses wrong scale/zero point.
2) KV cache reuse issue: cached keys/values quantized differently across steps (scale drift) leading to runaway attention logits -> NaN on softmax.
3) LayerNorm epsilon + casting: tiny eps + int8 rounding causes denorm/inf in variance calculation under some activation distributions.
4) Per-channel quantization mismatch between training calibration and runtime ordering (channel permutation bug).
5) Race condition in CUDA kernel when running batched vs single-batch path; non-deterministic NaN appearance suggests concurrency bug.

Debug artifacts collected:
- small dump of block6 activations for failing run: artifacts/block6_dump_fail.npy (uploaded to GH artifact for PR #345).
- full runtime logs: logs/nan-run-2026-03-18.txt (contains kernel warnings).
- calibration stats: calib/calib_stats_int8.json (shows per-channel scales, some channels have scale=0.0 -> suspicious).

Immediate repro experiments to run next:
- Add asserts to verify calibration scales > 0 before quantizing; log any channels with scale<1e-8.
- Force recomputation of KV cache every N steps (no reuse) to see if NaNs disappear; this isolates KV drift.
- Replace fp8-accel path with pure bf16 matmuls but keep int8 weights to test interaction.
- Run with torch.autograd.set_detect_anomaly(True) and CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 to catch kernel order issues (slow but helpful).

Quick patches tried locally (notes):
- Patch: if scale==0 -> set scale = 1e-7 to avoid division by zero; reduced NaN frequency but still fails on different prompt. So scale=0 is a contributor but not sole cause.
- Patch: cast inputs to float32 before layernorm and ensure eps=1e-3; helped but didn't fully fix.

Open TODOs / follow-ups:
- [ ] Reproduce minimal failing example (tiny model) that triggers NaN deterministically, to attach to GitHub.
- [ ] Add comprehensive unit tests for calibration step to ensure no zero scales and consistent channel ordering between quantize and runtime load.
- [ ] Pair with Lee on kernel tracing for fused-attn (look at assembly counters, check for divergent memory access patterns).
- [ ] Run inference with NVTX markers and per-kernel outputs to see which kernel produces first NaN.
- [ ] Investigate FP8 E4M3 vs E5M2 encoding differences; try switching FP8 format if available.

Notes for handoff (what I think):
- Start by validating calibration outputs (scales) and preventing scale==0. Also add logging of calibration channel ordering at both quantize time and runtime load time (hash of channel order).
- If calibration looks fine, then focus on fused-attn kernel: add intermediate dumps in GPU memory after fused-attn before softmax to detect NaN origin.
- If NaNs originate in softmax input (huge values), check accumulation dtype for attention score reduction (accum should be at least fp16/float32).

Scratch history (rough):
- 2026-03-18: first user incident reported in INF-1023 (customer saw NaN on hosted API when enabling "low-cost int8" mode).
- 2026-03-19: internal repro with FP8 accel toggles; intermittent NaNs reproduced.
- 2026-03-20: Maya initial triage + dumps, opened PR with logging + safety guards (PR 345).
- 2026-03-22: current scratchpad, added more experiments and test matrix.

If someone picks this up: start with calib_stats_int8.json and logs/nan-run-2026-03-18.txt. Ping Lee for kernel-level tracing. I'll keep iterating on minimal repro; will upload small-model failing checkpoint if/when I find deterministic case.

Quick copy-paste commands for whoever continues:
- Run slow debug:
  CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 python run_inference.py --model ./checkpoints/decoder_int8 --dtype int8 --enable-fp8-accel --debug-dump block6 --prompt-file examples/trigger.txt

- Force recompute KV:
  python run_inference.py --model ./checkpoints/decoder_int8 --dtype int8 --enable-fp8-accel --kv-mode recompute --prompt-file examples/trigger.txt

End of scratchpad.
